actors: The submitting firm, classified as a licensed corporation, SFC-licensed virtual asset service provider or associated entity.
The JFIU, which receives the STR.
Hongkong Post, identified as the issuer of the required e-Cert.
objects: One STR submission event to the JFIU.
The STR submitted in that event.
The channel used for that submission event.
The submission method: XML, upload of a completed prescribed PDF form, or completion of the STREAMS 2 web-based form.
The Hongkong Post e-Cert associated with an XML or PDF submission.
relationships: The submitting firm submits the identified STR to the JFIU through a particular channel at a particular time.
The submission channel and submission method are distinct: an XML or PDF document alone does not establish use of STREAMS 2.
Footnote 3 attaches to the XML and PDF alternatives; the supplied text does not attach it to the web-based alternative.
The e-Cert requirement concerns the particular submission, rather than unrelated possession of a certificate by the firm.
proposals.unit_of_assessment: One submission event by one classified licensed firm to the JFIU, including a resubmission if that is the event selected. The result assesses only the channel, listed submission method and footnote 3 requirement for that event.
proposals.temporal_basis: Apply at or after the stated STREAMS 2 launch at 9:00am on 2 February 2026. The blackout runs from 12:00am on 28 January 2026 until that launch. Boolean temporal classification is supplied from the event time because the expression fragment has dates but no time-of-day type. The source does not expressly identify a timezone.
classification_assumptions: The firm's classification as a licensed firm is supplied as an assessed fact using the categories in the circular.
The specific launch and blackout provisions qualify the general effective-date wording: the post-launch channel test is not applied to the portion of 2 February 2026 before 9:00am.
Each assessment identifies one submission event and its actual method. Multiple submission attempts are assessed separately.

Footnote 3 requires an applicable Hongkong Post e-Cert for XML and prescribed-PDF submissions. For this proposal, the certificate fact records an e-Cert made available for the particular submission; the source alone does not establish signing, authentication or attachment mechanics.

The result covers only the selected channel, method and e-Cert conditions. It does not assess XML-schema conformity, technical testing, reporting deadlines, substantive STR adequacy or overall legal compliance.
missing_information: What is the submitting firm's classification, and what evidence establishes it?
What is the event's exact time, and which timezone governs the stated launch and blackout times?
Which channel and submission method did this event actually use?
For an XML or PDF event, what evidence establishes that the required Hongkong Post e-Cert was available for this submission, and what certificate-use mechanics does the JFIU require?
If the event occurred during the blackout, did the STR require urgent submission, and what direct contact with the JFIU occurred?

reading.subject: Post-launch STR channel, submission-method and footnote 3 conditions
reading.statement: [TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT] Within scope, the result answers whether this individual submission event satisfies the selected STREAMS 2 channel, listed submission-method and footnote 3 e-Cert conditions under the stated certificate assumption. True means the event used STREAMS 2 and either used XML with the required e-Cert, uploaded a completed prescribed PDF form with the required e-Cert, or completed the STREAMS 2 web-based STR form. False means at least one of these selected conditions failed. A false or unknown scope produces no compliance judgment, and unknown input facts must not be treated as false. This is a proposed limited model, not legal approval.
reading.distinction: Channel, document format, form completion and submission-specific certificate provision are separate facts. A single Boolean such as submitted_electronically would conceal both an XML or PDF submission outside STREAMS 2 and the absence of an e-Cert for those methods. Calendar-date-only scope would also wrongly extend the channel rule into the pre-launch blackout on 2 February.

citations.quote: licensed corporations, SFC-licensed virtual asset service providers and associated entities (collectively referred to as “licensed firms”)
With effect from 2 February 2026, STREAMS 2 will become the only channel for filing STRs2. Licensed firms are required to submit STRs to the JFIU via STREAMS 2 by one of the following means:
submission of an STR in an Extensible Markup Language (XML) format3;
uploading a completed STR form in the prescribed PDF format3; or
completing the web-based STR form in STREAMS 2.
Hongkong Post e-Cert (electronic certificate) is required for this submission.
the JFIU will cease accepting STR submissions via STREAMS at 12:00am on 28 January 2026, and will resume accepting STR submissions at 9:00am on 2 February 2026 via STREAMS 2
for any STRs requiring urgent submission during the blackout period of STREAMS, please contact the JFIU directly by email (jfiu@police.gov.hk), phone at 2866 3366 or fax at 2529 4013;
upon the launch of STREAMS 2 at 9:00am on 2 February 2026, the operation of STREAMS will be discontinued.

assumptions: The firm's classification as a licensed firm is supplied as an assessed fact using the categories in the circular.
The specific launch and blackout provisions qualify the general effective-date wording: the post-launch channel test is not applied to the portion of 2 February 2026 before 9:00am.
Each assessment identifies one submission event and its actual method. Multiple submission attempts are assessed separately.

Footnote 3 requires an applicable Hongkong Post e-Cert for XML and prescribed-PDF submissions. For this proposal, the certificate fact records an e-Cert made available for the particular submission; the source alone does not establish signing, authentication or attachment mechanics.

The result covers only the selected channel, method and e-Cert conditions. It does not assess XML-schema conformity, technical testing, reporting deadlines, substantive STR adequacy or overall legal compliance.
questions: What is the submitting firm's classification, and what evidence establishes it?
What is the event's exact time, and which timezone governs the stated launch and blackout times?
Which channel and submission method did this event actually use?
For an XML or PDF event, what evidence establishes that the required Hongkong Post e-Cert was available for this submission, and what certificate-use mechanics does the JFIU require?
If the event occurred during the blackout, did the STR require urgent submission, and what direct contact with the JFIU occurred?

The JFIU, which receives the original submission and provides resubmission guidance.

Urgent direct contact during the blackout is temporally distinct from an off-platform submission following implementation.
proposals.unit_of_assessment: One original STR submission event by one classified licensed firm. Evaluate each original event separately; the formula does not aggregate all reports or determine whether a later resubmission discharged an obligation.
proposals.temporal_basis: Classify the original event against implementation at 9:00am on 2 February 2026, rather than using the date of a later resubmission or the date of assessment. The trigger remains a historical fact if a subsequent resubmission occurs.

Footnote 2 establishes a separate resubmission requirement, not permission to choose another post-launch reporting channel.
The supplied text does not establish a resubmission deadline or expressly extend footnote 2 to urgent blackout submissions.

reading.subject: Historical trigger for the separate STREAMS 2 resubmission requirement
reading.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] Within scope, the result answers whether the identified original STR submission triggers footnote 2's separate requirement to resubmit the same STR through STREAMS 2. True means the original event occurred at or after implementation and used a channel other than STREAMS 2. False means that specific trigger is absent. The result does not determine whether resubmission has occurred, whether an obligation remains outstanding, or whether the original event was compliant. Unknown facts remain unknown. This proposed interpretation confers no legal approval.
reading.distinction: A report-level Boolean such as submitted_via_streams2 could become true after resubmission and conceal the original off-platform event that triggered the obligation. Separating the original and subsequent events preserves both the initial channel assessment and the remedial requirement. It also prevents blackout contact from being classified as a post-launch off-platform submission solely because the report was later entered in STREAMS 2.

for any STRs requiring urgent submission during the blackout period of STREAMS, please contact the JFIU directly by email (jfiu@police.gov.hk), phone at 2866 3366 or fax at 2529 4013;

unresolved: No prior models were supplied for a missing-schema challenge. Internal inspection identified consequential distinctions between channel and method, submission and contact, report and submission event, original event and resubmission, and calendar date and launch instant. The second proposal addresses the event-history distinction without asserting an unsupported rival interpretation.

Retain the blackout urgent-contact exception as a separate conditional instruction: for an STR requiring urgent submission during the blackout, contact the JFIU by the stated email, phone or fax. Neither proposed result tests performance of this instruction. Direct contact does not by itself establish successful filing, and the post-launch exclusive-channel rule is not applied within the blackout.

The precise operational meaning of the e-Cert requirement remains unresolved. The first proposal is conditional on its explicit certificate-availability assumption; it cannot establish that mere availability suffices under technical requirements absent from the supplied text.

The permitted expression fragment cannot compare timestamps directly. Temporal facts must be established externally with the launch time and governing timezone preserved; a date-only comparison would lose a consequential boundary.

The resubmission trigger is representable, but timely discharge is not specified sufficiently to model: the supplied source gives no deadline and refers to further JFIU guidance. What timing and completion evidence does that guidance require?
The four dependency identifiers have no supplied contents or source hashes. No requirements from those missing materials, the separate XML schema or further JFIU guidance have been inferred.
